Aṁśumān
(‘endowed with light’)
------------------------------------------
Emperor सगर of Sūryavaṁśa (race descended from the sun) once started the अश्वमेध sacrifice (horse-sacrifice). When the sacrificial horse was lost, his sons went out in search of it and found it grazing in the monastery of the sage कपिल. The disrespect shown by them to the sage resulted in their being reduced to ashes. अṁशुमान् the grandson of सगर then set out in search of the horse and his uncles. When he discovered the horse and the tragedy, he pacified the sage and brought back the horse so that सगर could complete the sacrifice without further hitch. After the completion of the sacrifice, अṁशुमान् became the king and ruled for some time. Then he left his kingdom in charge of his son दिलीप and retired to the forest to perform austerities. He tried to bring the river गङ्गा to wash the ashes of his ancestors and redeem their souls, but he did not succeed. The task was achieved later by his grandson भगीरथ.
See also BHAGĪRATHA.
